---
title: Building an AAT (Agent-Action-Target) graph
---


The [`aat`](https://github.com/neelsmith/aat) package defines a reductive model of natural language syntax focusing only on Agent-Action-Target relations, instantiated in an `AATGraph`. You can construct an `AATGraph` from an `arsgrammatica` analysis with the `attgraph` function.

Load a [saved analysis](./saving-loading.qmd), or analyze some Latin text:

```python
from arsgrammatica import analyze_string
sentences, results = analyze_string("Troia et huic loco nomen est.", citation="Livy 1.1.4:")
```

You can then construct an `AATGraph` from the resulting sentences and analyses.

```python
from arsgrammatica import attgraph
graph, warnings = attgraph(sentences, results)
```

For more information about AAT graphs, see the [`aat` github repository](https://github.com/neelsmith/aat).

## A graph-theoretic note

AAT graphs (like UD graphs) are guaranteed to be *trees*. While `arsgrammatica`'s syntax graphs tend to approximate a tree structure, they may include doubly linked nodes (like *que* in this example), and are not guaranteed to be *acyclic*.

AAT graphs, like `arsgrammatica`'s graphs, are directed towards root-level verbal elements.
